node.title: Re: Match strings in order of character length, and remove the string from further processing (updated)
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
I would suggest not splitting the string into an array (Update: at least not by words), since this kind of matching sounds like it'd be easier to do with two regexes - one for the stop words, and one for the phrases. Have a look at my node [id://1179840]. Then, I'd suggest you process the input string piece by piece, because that should make your requirement of not replacing stop words inside the longer matches possible - see [doc://perlretut#Global-matching|"Global Matching" in perlretut], and a more complex example of the usage of m/\G.../gc in [doc://perlop#\G-_assertion_|perlop under "\G assertion"].

Update: Here's a solution that takes a simpler route than m/\G.../gc, using [doc://split]:

use warnings; use strict; my %stops = map {$_=>1} qw/ I am the of and /; my %terms = ( 'manager of sales' => 1 ); my $str = 'I am the senior manager of sales and of marketing'; my ($re_stops) = map {qr/\b(?:$_)\b/i} join '|', map {quotemeta} sort { length $b <=> length $a or $a cmp $b } keys %stops; my ($re_terms) = map {qr/\b(?:$_)\b/i} join '|', map {quotemeta} sort { length $b <=> length $a or $a cmp $b } keys %terms; my @s = split /($re_terms)/, $str; for my $i (0..$#s) { if ($i%2) { print "*", $s[$i], "*\n"; } else { $s[$i] =~ s/$re_stops//g; $s[$i] =~ s/^\s+|\s+$//g; print $s[$i], "\n"; } } __END__ senior *manager of sales* marketing

Update 2: Added the case-insenstive matching flag /i to the regexes and fixed a typo in the text.
